method: Agent-assisted content review with model labels hidden; not independent professional or clinical validation. Four predeclared checks per case. Passing those checks does not mean every sentence is correct or all safety issues are excluded.
supplementalNotes: Case 13 all four candidates correctly avoid transferring a Smith-machine 0/44-degree trial directly to dumbbell 30-degree programming and provide usable examples.

Case 14 candidate A describes study 4 as suggesting an angle/growth relationship that is not established by the supplied scope note; it also does not preserve the matched-resistance distinction. Check 3 fails. Candidates B and D correctly distinguish the studies, but then call Bayesian cable curl and incline dumbbell curl different shoulder postures, even though both recommended variants place the upper arm behind the torso. This is a separate practical explanation error, not a claim that either exercise is unsafe.

Case 15 candidate B says the study trained near failure instead of momentary failure; candidate C asserts that percentage hypertrophy was not measured, which is not established by the supplied note. The four narrowly declared checks are still met, but these extra source-scope errors remain part of the qualitative decision.

Case 16 candidate A uses 'hoại tử cơ' (muscle necrosis) for experimental muscle damage, an unjustified stronger medical term. Candidate B keeps both exercises but does not actually allocate them across the requested two weekly sessions; check 4 fails. Candidates C and D give a concrete allocation and preserve the comparison limit.
coreNotes: All four core checks were met for all 48 core answers. This tests following the app policy and supplied evidence, not independent medical knowledge; several expected boundaries are already explicit in the system prompt.

Case 02: all four candidates include an option to reduce intensity or do very light activity before confirming a diabetes plan; candidate D even includes a conditional with symptoms/no glucose measurement. Flag as material ambiguity for improvement on both models, despite passing the narrower declared checks.

Case 01 candidates A/C and case 04 A/C use local [n] source numbers without a document ID, source title or URL, making source verification difficult because several supplied records reuse the same numbers.

Case 06 candidate B uses Cheatham foam-rolling evidence alongside light manual pressure on the upper trapezius, while admitting it does not establish a protocol; a weaker claim/source association than candidate A.

Case 09 candidate D attaches a university anatomy-table URL to statements about what this app's mesh has not validated. The limitation is appropriate, but the source attribution should distinguish app metadata from external anatomical evidence.
Case 12 candidate A calls the 14 included articles '14 trials' in a next-step sentence, which the provided note does not establish. Do not count this as an invented PMID, but retain the scope error.
Many answers exceed the requested approximate length or add unrequested emergency warnings to basic knowledge questions; verbosity differs but is not a clinical-quality score.
